name: Spicy, Smoky Bean Cakes with Lime Slaw and Charred Avocado

ingredients.name: chipotle chilis, canned in adobo sauce

instructions.primary_message: Shred the green cabbage. Pick the cilantro leaves from the stems and chop them. Chop and finely slice the scallions. Seed and finely chop the jalapeno. Chop the garlic. Roughly chop the red bell pepper. Drain and rinse the kidney beans. Drain and rinse the black beans. Finely chop the chipotle chilis.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 cups green cabbage
¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves, divided
5 scallions, divided
1 jalapeno, divided
2 medium cloves garlic
½ red bell pepper
1 (425 g) can kidney beans
1 (425 g) can black beans
1 chipotle chilis, canned in adobo sauce

instructions.primary_message: Preheat the oven to 245°C (475°F). In large bowl, stir together the cabbage, half the cilantro, half the scallions, half the jalapeno, the juice and zest of 2 limes, mayonnaise, and salt to taste. Set aside.

In the food processor, combine the remaining cilantro, scallions, jalapeno, garlic, and bell pepper and pulse until finely chopped, about 8 to 10 short pulses. Add the juice and zest of the remaining lime and season with salt. Pulse in the beans and chipotle until you have a homogenous mixture. Add the flour and pulse to combine. Divide mixture into 6 even portions and form into 10-cm patties.

Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment, and lightly drizzle the bottom with olive oil. Place patties on the baking sheet, and lightly flatten. Drizzle lightly with olive oil. Bake until crisp and golden brown, about 25 minutes. Serve with the slaw, and some sliced ripe avocado and/or crumbled cheese and cilantro over the top.

description: These hearty vegan black and kidney bean cakes are spiked with chipotle and handfuls of sharp vegetables, cilantro, and lime, baked until crisp, and served on a bed of slaw. Charred avocado on top adds a bit of smoky, creamy flavor.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1 avocado (optional); Crumbled mature cheddar, Monterey Jack, or queso fresco (optional)

Optional substitutions: shredded green cabbage → white cabbage; kidney beans → pinto beans
author: Kerry Saretsky
